object_description: large stepped volume with courtyards and a sunken gymnasium
design_condition: A single large volume occupies the northern part of the plot, preserving southern expansion space and weaving the clinic into the park, although its footprint and topographic placement remain problematic.

positive.statement: The carefully structured volume with setbacks and courtyards is attractive.

position.rationale: The large stepped footprint and internal courtyard voids are clearly visible in the top view.

positive.statement: The landscape concept successfully integrates the existing clinic into an overarching outdoor-space system.

position.rationale: The southern open area provides the strongest plausible anchor for the integrated landscape system.

positive.statement: The oval outdoor areas naturally weave the clinic into the park landscape.

position.rationale: Outdoor areas are approximated within the open southern landscape around the main volume.

positive.statement: The main entrance and forecourt provide clear addressing.

position.rationale: The likely public approach is anchored on the open southern edge facing the preserved expansion area.

positive.statement: The central staircase enables easy orientation through the three floors.

position.rationale: A central vertical connector is approximated within the courtyard-forming central mass.

positive.statement: The circuit organization offers different movement paths and additional exposure.

position.rationale: Movement circuits are internal and not directly visible, so the connected central building mass is used.

positive.statement: The southern area remains available for a coherently integrated later expansion.

position.rationale: The open southern zone is visibly distinct from the large northern building footprint.

negative.statement: The sunken gymnasium and its projecting skylight lanterns appear strange in the situation.

position.rationale: The lowered gymnasium is approximated within the central building mass; lanterns are not separately identifiable.

negative.statement: The seemingly oversized paved access area is criticized.

position.rationale: The expansive southern approach zone is the plausible location for the criticized paved access.

negative.statement: Rooms arranged around the courtyards create undesirable corridors with dark endings.

position.rationale: Courtyard voids and surrounding perimeter bands are visibly identifiable, though corridor darkness is internal.

negative.statement: The ward room at the children's ward entrance is operationally disadvantageous.

position.target: ward room at children's ward entrance
position.rationale: The entrance-side room is approximated near the southern approach within the stepped footprint.

negative.statement: The school arrangement removes the everyday route to school, which is regrettable and undesirable.

position.rationale: The missing everyday route is anchored between the southern approach and the building entrance.

negative.statement: The terrace and connecting walkways above the entrance courtyard are unthinkable.

position.rationale: Upper connections above the entrance courtyard are approximated along the southern upper building edge.

negative.statement: The youth outdoor area can only be reached via stairs.

position.rationale: The youth area is placed in the southern open zone, with stair access not directly visible.

negative.statement: The large footprint leaves the topographic positioning unresolved and raises questions about the visible roof landscape.

position.target: large footprint and visible roof landscape
position.rationale: The broad roofed footprint and stepped massing are clearly visible, while topographic resolution remains uncertain.
